summary.title: The microarchitecture of Intel, AMD, and VIA CPUs
summary.one_liner: A long optimization guide by Agner Fog that explains how x86 CPU cores from Intel, AMD, and VIA are built internally, from branch prediction and out-of-order execution to decoding and pipelines, to help assembly programmers and compiler makers write faster code.
takeaways: The guide covers the pipeline, decoding, and branch prediction of x86 cores from the Pentium 1 through recent Intel, AMD Zen, and VIA Nano designs.
Each processor family has its own section on fetch, decode, micro-op cache or loop buffer, register renaming, execution units, and bottlenecks.
It is aimed at assembly programmers and compiler makers who want to tune code for specific CPU behaviour.
The table of contents indicates sections on branch prediction per microarchitecture, including AMD K8/K10, Bulldozer family, Zen, and Bobcat/Jaguar.
summary.summary: This is a long reference manual by Agner Fog, last updated 2026-05-23, that documents the internal microarchitecture of x86 CPUs from Intel, AMD, and VIA. It is organised chronologically by processor family, from the Pentium 1 and Pentium 4 through Core 2, Sandy Bridge, Haswell, Skylake, Ice Lake, Alder Lake, Atom, and Silvermont, with sections on AMD K8/K10, Bulldozer, Zen, and VIA Nano. Each family is broken down into fetch and decoding, micro-op cache or loop buffer, register renaming, execution units, store forwarding, and known bottlenecks. The excerpt provided shows only the table of contents, so the specific misprediction penalty and micro-op cache measurements mentioned in the listing could not be verified from this text.
